vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ui-craft-pro
Version: 0.1.8

The ui-craft-pro skill bundle is a legitimate UI/UX design assistant that provides a structured workflow for generating design systems and implementation code. The Python scripts (scripts/core.py, scripts/design_system.py, scripts/search.py) implement a local BM25 search engine over a comprehensive set of UI/UX data stored in CSV files. The bundle lacks any indicators of malicious intent, such as data exfiltration, network calls, or obfuscation; the file-writing capability in design_system.py is a documented feature for persisting design documentation (MASTER.md) within the user's project directory.

llm.summary: The skill's files and instructions mostly match a local design-tool workflow, but there are notable inconsistencies (path mismatches, duplicated files) and a flagged 'system-prompt-override' pattern in SKILL.md that warrant manual review before installing or running.

dimensions.detail: The package contains a large local design knowledge base (CSV data) and Python scripts to search/generate design systems and map them to code, which is coherent with the UI-design purpose. However, SKILL.md invokes commands under 'skills/ui-craft-pro/scripts/...' while the manifest lists scripts at 'scripts/...', creating a path mismatch. The presence of many large CSVs and reference docs is proportionate to a design assistant.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run local Python scripts (e.g. python3 skills/ui-craft-pro/scripts/search.py) and to read/derive design tokens from many CSVs — that's expected. However: (1) SKILL.md was flagged by a pre-scan for a 'system-prompt-override' pattern (prompt-injection), which is not expected for a design skill and should be inspected; (2) the command paths in SKILL.md don't match the file manifest, which could cause the agent to run unexpected commands or fail; (3) the instructions give broad discretion to 'use the result to drive implementation' which is reasonable for design but could be interpreted loosely by an autonomous agent — review any open-ended instruction text that could cause unexpected filesystem or network access.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (no downloads or external package installation), which reduces supply-chain risk. All code and data are included in the bundle; nothing in the provided snippet indicates fetching code from arbitrary URLs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The included data files appear to be design assets and CSV knowledge-bases appropriate to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not forced-always and uses default invocation rules (user-invocable, agent may invoke autonomously). It does not request system-wide configuration or other skills' credentials. No 'always: true' privilege abuse is present.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before you install or run this skill:

- Inspect SKILL.md fully for any text that tries to change the agent's system role or give global/system-level instructions (the pre-scan flagged a 'system-prompt-override' pattern). If you find any 'set system prompt' or similar lines, treat them as suspicious.
- Verify the file paths and invocation commands. SKILL.md expects scripts under skills/ui-craft-pro/scripts/, but the manifest lists scripts/ at the package root. Confirm where the scripts will run from; this mismatch can cause failures or accidental execution of the wrong files.
- Manually review the Python scripts (search.py, core.py, design_system.py, style_signature.py and _sync_all.py) for any network calls (requests, urllib, socket, subprocess), writes to unexpected filesystem locations, or code that reads sensitive files outside the skill directory. Pay particular attention to any subprocess.exec/ Popen usage or calls to external endpoints.
- Because there is no install step, running the skill implies executing included Python code. If you plan to run it, do so in an isolated environment (sandbox/container) and with a non-privileged user until you're comfortable with its behavior.
- Confirm that python3 is available in your environment (SKILL.md examples call python3 but the skill metadata doesn't list python as a required binary). If you don't want to execute code, you can still use the CSV/reference files as read-only design material.

If you want, I can: (a) scan the visible Python files for network/subprocess patterns and summarize findings, or (b) search SKILL.md for the exact prompt-injection text and quote it so you can judge whether it's benign documentation or an active override attempt.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] unexpected: The SKILL.md content triggered a prompt-injection pattern scanner for 'system-prompt-override'. A UI-design skill should not need to override agent/system prompts. Inspect SKILL.md for any lines attempting to set or replace system/assistant roles, or that embed special instructions intended to manipulate the host agent's system message.
